newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty rises vs basket, wary of c.bank intervention.
newsitem.headline: Zloty rises vs basket, wary of c.bank intervention.

text.p: The Polish zloty rose against the basket of currencies in early trade as small exporters orders fell in step with banks selling currencies to keep higher yielding zloty positions over the weekend, dealers said.
They said however, the market may decide not to push the zloty too high to avoid a central bank intervention.
"The zloty is on the rise because of traditional Wednesday currency position shortening and small exporter orders," said Mateusz Bieniek of Societe Generale in Warsaw.
At 0750 GMT the zloty was at3.16/3.13 percent from the trading band centre against 3.08/3.00 percent at opening.
The central bank last intervened against the zloty at 3.1 percent from the parity rate, but it has also recently let it firm to above 3.2 percent without taking any action.
"It is a mystery when the NBP will step in," said Tomasz Nowakowski of Bank Handlowy SA.
The zloty was at 3.1230/40 against the dollar and 1.8093/98 against the mark against the opening 3.1265/90 and 1.8100/15 respectively.
Dealers did not expect potential foreign investor entry into Polish T-bills at today's 400 million zloty tender to be big enough to give the zloty a further boost.
"Many foreign investors already keep zloty accounts so they don't have to rush to sell dollars to pay for T-bills when the time comes," said Piotr Czyzewski of ING Bank in Warsaw.
Dealers expected T-bill yields to stay flat today's tender after better then expected March inflation data and after the treasury showed it would not accept lower prices during previous auctions.
Inflation was 0.8 percent in March, against market expectations of 1.44 percent, taking the year-on-year index down to 16.6 percent.

Call money rates eased to 22.10/22.50 percent in morning trade despite a net 31 million zloty outflow from the system and dealers said bids could touch 22.00 percent later today, but were puzzled by the higher liquidity.
They expect the National Bank of Poland to stage a 200 million zloty reverse repo and a 300 million zloty NBP bill sale to underpin rates.
They said the bank signalled it still wanted high market rates after it raised the average yield of its 91-day bills by 0.02 point to 22.17 percent at Tuesday's sale.
